q: Someone told me the website was down that day. Can you tell if that's true?
tool_errors: metrics_query: {"error":"Granularity 'hour' is not available for metric 'page_views' (view 'web_events' has no intraday timestamp axis). Use granularity 'day', or query an hourly-capable metric such as orders / total_sales on commerce_orders."}
answer:
No — there’s no sign the site was down on 9 Oct. Sessions were recorded every hour that day and total page views (7,623) were essentially unchanged from 8 Oct (7,740), so traffic continued reaching the site.

- What I checked: hourly sessions (Snowplow sessions) show traffic in every hour on 2026-10-09 (top hours: 10:00–13:00 had 287–411 sessions) — no multi-hour gaps or zeroes that indicate an outage.  
- Totals: page views were 7,623 on 9 Oct vs 7,740 on 8 Oct (no large drop), so the drop in sales cannot be explained by the site being unavailable.  
- Limitations: this uses session and page-view instrumentation (Snowplow / web events). If the tracking pixel itself failed to fire while the site was up, sessions could be undercounted; however the hourly continuity argues against a full tracking or site outage.  

Worth checking: landing-page errors or checkout errors for the hours when conversion fell (10:00–14:00); also look at server-side error logs for 9 Oct if you want a definitive infrastructure check.
